newsitem.title: LEBANON: Hizbollah says Katyushas to save ceasefire deal.
newsitem.headline: Hizbollah says Katyushas to save ceasefire deal.

text.p: Hizbollah Chief Sheikh Hassan Nasrallah said on Tuesday that Katyusha rocketing of northern Israel aimed at restoring the terms of a 1996 ceasefire which barred targeting of civilians.

Nasrallah dismissed as laughable the Israeli explanation that the Jewish state was not responsible for Monday's shelling of the Lebanese port city of Sidon by militiamen of the pro-Israeli Christian commander Antoine Lahd. Seven civilians were killed in the shelling.

"We will not accept the equation of security for civilians in northern Israel and death for civilians in south Lebanon," he told reporters hours after his group fired dozens of Katyusha rockets into northern Israeli settlements.
"What we have done brings back life to the understanding which the Israelis buried months ago," he added.
The U.S.-brokered ceasefire understanding ended a 17-day Israeli onslaught on Lebanon in which 200 people -- mostly civilians -- were killed in April 1996.
Israel, which occupies a border strip in south Lebanon, said Lahd forces responsible for shelling Sidon were based in Jezzine area outside the zone and were not under its control.
It said Lahd's men were apparently avenging the killing of three youths by a roadside bomb in the area. The Israeli army accused the pro-Iranian Hizbollah of carrying out that attack.

Nasrallah said: "Antoine Lahd is a tool for Israel. What Antoine Lahd does, Israel is completely responsible for. Talk of control over Lahd or lack of total control is sarcastic and makes even the children of Lebanon laugh."
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu threatened a tough response to Hizbollah's Katyusha attack which lightly wounded an Israeli civilian early on Tuesday.

"The Islamic Resistance...fired dozens of Katyusha rockets into the settlements in northern Palestine to tell the Israelis that the response to Sidon's massacres will not be in Jezzine or in the border zone or against our Lebanese people but rather against northern Palestine," Nasrallah said.
"We call on the enemy to read with extreme care our morning message," he added, referring to the Katyusha attacks.
